<!-- pr-reviewer: 7b645e1884096c242693552c3072eebe38326538 -->
Gap verdict: may merge — the stock-edge-line mismatch is a read-level difference between the kernel's own read space and the #4154 meter on the converted toolpath (the kernel cannot see the entry, stage 5), not a silent unguarded cut: law 6 refuses an unnamed read in the kernel's own read space and is green on this head; the measured gap is pinned, documented in the design record and filed as P7 #4260.
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

## What looks good
- One stage, one law: the load stage reads with a single engagement law in the cut order (`load/law.rs`) and every mode goes through it; `Controlled::new` stays the single gate for law 6 (`load.rs:204-217`).
- The negative pins are real: an unnamed over-limit cut, a bad limit (NaN, -0.1, 0, 1.5), a tool radius that is not a number, and the stock reach of constant engagement are each refused by name (`load_stage.rs:186-201`).
- No old planner changes: the default switch is identical (all the K4 tests untouched and green). No new `camcraft-*` dependency; 11 files, docs + tests + `load/*`, no Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/scripts/`.github`/`xtask` changes.
- Provenance comments on every new module; new test files join existing directory suites (`laws/load_stage.rs`, `kernel_laws/k3_load.rs`); the design record is present and links the follow-up.

## Results (locally, worktree off `pr-4265-review` on base `origin/side/path-kernel` 7f70d8b1a; not the runner)
Trial merge against `origin/side/path-kernel`: already up to date (the PR is a strict descendant of the base, no conflicts).

- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: **130 passed**, 0 failed (19.1s) — includes the 5 new K3 pins in `load_stage.rs` (all ok).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --lib`: **5 passed** (0 failed).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test kernel_laws`: **30 passed**, 0 failed (44.1s) — includes `kernel_load_control_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` (ok; the READ table is pinned exactly: disc Inside 3507/173/0, disc Outside 402/145/13, dog bone Inside 2587/173/0, dog bone Outside 724/167/3, CE disc Inside 833/173/1, disc Outside 334/118/74, dog bone Inside 581/173/1, dog bone Outside 678/143/66).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The quick plan (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel --dry-run`) maps the diff to exactly these suites: pathkernel lib, pathkernel laws, motion kernel_laws. Nothing else is mapped, so the example catalogs and the light lane in the PR body are the author's reported numbers, not re-run here; no post/toolpath/app code changed and no heavy lane is reached.

## Targeted tests and the safety floor
- Post/toolpath: no change to the old planner or the posted output ("with the default switch the output is identical"); the example-catalog and light-lane claims are the author's, not re-run.
- P2 (not a P1 under the safety floor): no targeted heavy step is owed. `load_stage.rs` pins law 6 in the kernel's own read space via `check_l6` (`tests/laws/load_stage.rs:84-101`, `check_l6` in `tests/laws/l6_load.rs:13-47`): each read above `limit x (1 + PLAN_TOL) + GRID_TOL` needs an over-limit record within one tool radius of the place. That is what "no named place within one tool radius" means in this PR, and the same notion is used in the motion pin (`kernel_laws/k3_load.rs:55-66`: an over-limit record within R of the move's place). The pins are green.

## Requested before merge
None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **The stock-edge-line gap (the ask).** In the kernel's own read space the stage is guarded: every cut above the limit gets an over-limit record or the set is refused, and the law-6 pins are green. The gap is visible to the #4154 meter on the converted toolpath: `k3_load` pins 13 unnamed over moves (disc Outside, None), 74 (CE), 3 and 66 (dog bone Outside), all at places on the stock edge line (y = -25 or x = -40) — the places where a piece starts after a lift. The kernel stage runs before the entry stage, so it cannot see the entry's bore and clears nothing at the piece start; the meter sweeps the plunge entry on the converted toolpath. The first read of a piece is without the entry's bore, which is why the kernel read (0.0-0.13) and the meter (>62.5 degrees) disagree there. Inside the difference is one unnamed move, a link feed, and no lifts anywhere (the Inside start starts at the part wall). The Inside rows are 0/1 unnamed. `docs/decisions/4026-kernel-load-control.md` documents this at the head ("The unnamed moves Outside are on the stock edge line... That is follow-up #4260 (P7)") and the PR body names it and #4260 (open, P7, effort:high: `gh issue view 4260`). The kernel control path is not dead: constant engagement lowers the meter's worst readings (disc Outside worst 145 → 118 deg, None 402 → CE 334 over moves), so the stage works; it is just blind to the stock-edge-line reading until stage 5 exists.
2. The constant-engagement cells get more unnamed moves than None (74 vs 13; 66 vs 3) even as the worst angle improves — more passes means more piece starts, hence more stock-edge-line reads. Worth one line in the #4260 note when it is worked; it is already implied by the pin.
3. The 5 new laws pins pass in 19.1s and the motion pin in 44.1s — both well inside the quick tier targets.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
